title: Pager/editor commands: split with shlex.split (POSIX mode) into an argv list, never shell=True

note.title: Pager/editor commands: split with shlex.split (POSIX mode) into an argv list, never shell=True
answers: editor path with spaces not found / EDITOR with quotes fails
why does click.edit not use shell=True
PAGER with quoted Windows path keeps quotes
filename with shell metacharacters runs commands when editing
note.body:
Symptom: `click.edit()` / `echo_via_pager` fail for EDITOR/PAGER values like `"C:\Program Files\...\sublime_text.exe" --wait` (quotes kept in the program name), or a filename containing `"; rm -rf /` is interpreted by a shell.
Root cause: src/click/_termui_impl.py:pager used `shlex.split(..., posix=False)`, which keeps quote characters in tokens; Editor.edit_files built one string `f"{editor} {quoted files}"` and ran it with `shell=True`.
Fix pattern: `shlex.split(cmd)` in default POSIX mode (strips quotes, honours `\ ` escapes), then append filenames as separate argv items: `Popen(args=shlex.split(editor) + list(filenames), env=environ)`. _pipepager/_tempfilepager resolve argv[0] with `shutil.which`; on Windows Popen re-quotes via list2cmdline.
Constraints: Do not reintroduce `shell=True`, string-concatenated commands, `posix=False`, or `shlex.quote` (a quote-based approach was reverted before). A reviewer questioned whether POSIX-mode shlex is correct on every platform (unescaped backslashes in unquoted Windows paths get eaten), so test Windows paths explicitly when changing this.
